source.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 in D major, BWV 1050 — III. Allegro
source.encoder: Joshua Koo; LilyPond 2.18 update and A–B–A corrections by Joram Berger

bars.description: Complete movement III, 310 engraved 2/4 bars in written order. The source’s repeat unfold constructs already write out the A–B–A return, with staggered staff-rest prefixes and alternatives; no additional repeat traversal is applied. The opening rests stay within bar 1, not an invented pickup.

endpoints.basis: The fresh 0.4–3.5 s pitch overlay and independent attacks at 0.940, 1.103 and 1.393 s identify the source opening A4–D5–A4 after 0.75 quarter of written rests. Reject the broad first window’s 1.38 s rise (peak 1.40 s): it selects the third note’s repeated A4 and compresses the first two notes to milliseconds despite passing numeric gates. Restrict the first anchor to the actual initial A4. The closing D-major sonority begins around 293.6 s in the 292–296.5 s overlay, including new D2 bass energy. Reject the initial broad last window’s 295.52 s decay fluctuation, which delayed the last attack and failed the 0.5 s anchor gate.

provenance: Only Mutopia 548’s complete movement-III score.ly and score.mid correspond to this recording. Individual practice-part MIDIs and movements I or II are not substituted.

The source names flute, principal violin, ripieno violin, viola, cello, violone and the two harpsichord source variables. Isolated compilation preserves harpsichord cross-staff ownership; labels follow source definitions rather than anonymous MIDI track names or General MIDI patches. Aggregate source pitch/onset identity is asserted against score.mid before any explicit sounding-pitch correction.

Joram Berger’s source-header note identifies the 2015 A–B–A refactoring and correction of discrepant returning notes. Source unfold repeats already generate 620 quarter units, so the 310-bar canonical timeline is used once.

The Violone source has no written MIDI transposition. MEAS: an independent ffmpeg/Welch spectrum at 187–191 s has a strongest low peak at 68.637 Hz (C♯2), 9.12 dB above the 139.293 Hz C♯3 peak. During source quarters 394–404.5, Violone alone sustains C♯3 continuously; cello C♯3 attacks last only 0.5 quarters every two quarters, and the harpsichord moves through pitches 49–62. No source part is below MIDI 49. The overlay shows sustained MIDI-37 energy under this pedal. INFERENCE: a 16-foot realisation best represents the written Violone line, so only that part is lowered 12 semitones in sounding events; the written engraving remains unchanged. This is not inferred from its contrabass patch. The physical bass instrument and harpsichord registration remain undocumented; a 16-foot keyboard stop could also contribute. The lowest F♯1/G1/A1 fundamentals are weak.

Figured-bass symbols are retained in the engraving but are not converted into invented continuo notes. Written trill indications, chord holds and source durations are not a transcription of performed ornament attacks or releases.
